body: What best describes the cracked bell’s status at the end of the passage?
options: He returns it to the doorway to announce visitors.
He discards it because it is cracked.
He takes it away from the shop for storage.
He keeps it in the shop without requiring it to announce visitors.
explanation: The shopkeeper places the cracked bell beside the till, and the passage states that it can remain part of the shop without doing its former work. Option D captures both its continued presence in the shop and the end of its visitor-announcing role.
passage_text: For years, the brass bell above the shop door had announced every visitor. When it cracked, the shopkeeper fitted a quieter bell. His daughter liked being able to hear a conversation without interruption. He still turned towards the door before the new bell rang, expecting the old sound. One evening, he placed the cracked bell beside the till rather than returning it to the doorway. A customer lifted it gently and recognised its worn handle. The shopkeeper smiled. The old bell could remain part of the shop without being required to do its former work.
evidence_quotes: cracked bell beside the till rather than returning it to the doorway. A customer lifted it gently and recognised its worn handle. The shopkeeper smiled. The old bell could remain part of the shop without being required to do its former work.
stated_assumptions: The supplied passage is the sole evidence for the item.
The question asks about the bell’s status at the end of the passage.
option_analysis: A is incorrect: the shopkeeper places the bell beside the till rather than returning it to the doorway.
B is incorrect: the bell remains beside the till as part of the shop; it is not discarded.
C is incorrect: the bell is placed inside the shop beside the till, not taken away.
D is correct: the bell remains part of the shop without being required to do its former work.

body:
Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
(A) Each member then practised the assigned part individually.
(B) Finally, they performed the scene together using the parts they had practised.
(C) At a fictional rehearsal, the group first read a short scene together.
(D) After reading it, they assigned its speaking parts.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
(A) C-A-D-B
(B) D-C-A-B
(C) C-D-A-B
(D) C-D-B-A
explanation: The account reports that the group first read the scene, assigned its parts after reading, practised those assigned parts, and finally performed the scene using the practised parts. Therefore, the coherent order is C-D-A-B. This is the sequence of events in the stated account, not a claim about all rehearsals.
evidence_quotes: At a fictional rehearsal, the group first read a short scene together. After reading it, they assigned its speaking parts. Each member then practised the assigned part individually. Finally, they performed the scene together using the parts they had practised. This is the reported sequence of events rather than a claim
that all rehearsals must follow the same procedure.
stated_assumptions: The sentences are to be ordered as events in the fictional rehearsal account.
The account reports this rehearsal's sequence and does not claim that every rehearsal follows the same procedure.
option_analysis: Option A places individual practice before the assignment of speaking parts, contrary to the reported sequence.
Option B places the assignment of parts before the group reads the scene, contrary to the reported sequence.
Option C follows the reported order: reading, assigning parts, individual practice, and performing.
Option D places the performance before the individual practice, contrary to the reported sequence.

body:
Match List-I with List-II. Each entry in List-I is to be matched with one entry in List-II, and each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) A reply is aggressive or unfriendly, and its speaker is ready to argue.
(B) An event occurs only occasionally, at irregular intervals.
(C) A household uses only as much money as is necessary.
(D) An item is known to be genuine and not a copy.

List-II
(I) Hostile
(II) Sporadic
(III) Frugal
(IV) Authentic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: An aggressive or unfriendly reply from someone ready to argue is hostile. An event occurring occasionally at irregular intervals is sporadic; using only the necessary amount of money is frugal; and something genuine rather than a copy is authentic. These meanings give the complete matching in option A.
evidence_quotes: aggressive or unfriendly and ready to argue or fight
happening only occasionally or at intervals that are not regular
using only as much money or food as is necessary
known to be real and what somebody claims it is, and not a copy
stated_assumptions: Each List-I description is intended to express the defining meaning of one List-II word.
option_analysis: Correct: the aggressive or unfriendly reply is hostile; the irregularly occasional event is sporadic; necessary spending is frugal; and the genuine item is authentic.
Incorrect: it swaps hostile and sporadic, although readiness to argue describes hostile and irregular, occasional occurrence describes sporadic.
Incorrect: it matches the irregularly occurring event with frugal and necessary spending with sporadic, contrary to their stated meanings.
Incorrect: it matches necessary spending with authentic and the genuine item with frugal, contrary to their stated meanings.

paying careful attention to every detail
liking to be with other people
failing to notice signs of danger or trouble

C describes a preference for company, which does not contrast with noticing danger signs.
D describes failing to notice danger signs, the opposite of the sense of "vigilant" used in the context.

body:
Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
(A) She then attached the cut sheet to the board and let the adhesive dry.
(B) In a fictional class project, Tara first measured the width of the display board.
(C) Only after the adhesive had dried did she arrange the photographs on the covered board.
(D) Using that measurement, she cut a sheet of paper to fit the board.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: Sentence (B) introduces the measurement that sentence (D) refers to as “that measurement”. Sentence (D) introduces the cut sheet used in (A), while (C) places arranging the photographs after the adhesive has dried.
evidence_quotes: In a fictional class project, Tara first measured the width of the display board. Using that measurement, she cut a sheet of paper to fit it. She then attached the cut sheet to the board and let the adhesive dry. Only after it had dried did she arrange the photographs on the covered board. The account describes that
sequence explicitly; it does not prescribe a universal method of preparing every display.
stated_assumptions: All four sentences describe the same fictional class project.
The adhesive in sentence (C) is the adhesive mentioned in sentence (A).
option_analysis: Correct. (B) supplies the measurement used in (D); (D) introduces the cut sheet attached in (A); and (C) places the photographs after the adhesive has dried.
Incorrect. Sentence (A) refers to a cut sheet, but this order places it before sentence (D), which describes cutting the sheet.
Incorrect. Sentence (D) refers to “that measurement” before sentence (B) introduces the measurement.
Incorrect. Sentence (C) places arranging the photographs after the adhesive has dried, so it cannot precede sentence (A), which says the adhesive is then left to dry.

List-I
(A) During a discussion, Sam responds in an aggressive, unfriendly way and seems ready to argue.
(B) An explanation for missing a meeting seems reasonable and likely to be true.
(C) Lee behaves proudly and unpleasantly, showing little thought for others.
(D) Mira openly and honestly says what she thinks without hiding her thoughts.

List-II
(I) Candid
(II) Hostile
(III) Plausible
(IV) Arrogant

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Sam’s aggressive and unfriendly response, with readiness to argue, illustrates hostile. The explanation is plausible, Lee’s behaviour is arrogant, and Mira’s open and honest expression is candid.

behaving in a proud, unpleasant way, showing little thought for other people
saying what you think openly and honestly; not hiding your thoughts

Correct: it matches Sam’s response with hostile, the explanation with plausible, Lee’s behaviour with arrogant, and Mira’s expression with candid.
Incorrect: it pairs the reasonable explanation with arrogant and Lee’s behaviour with plausible.
Incorrect: it pairs the reasonable explanation with candid and Mira’s open, honest expression with plausible.

body: After the cracked bell was moved, what does the passage say about its role in the shop?
options: It was discarded because it could no longer ring.
It remained part of the shop without its former function.
It was returned to the doorway to announce every visitor.
It was repaired and fitted above the door as the quieter bell.
explanation: The passage says the old bell could remain part of the shop without being required to do its former work. Thus, it was kept but no longer used to announce visitors. The passage places it beside the till, not back at the doorway.
passage_text: For years, the brass bell above the shop door had announced every visitor. When it cracked, the shopkeeper fitted a quieter bell. His daughter liked being able to hear a conversation without interruption. He still turned towards the door before the new bell rang, expecting the old sound. One evening, he placed the cracked bell beside the till rather than returning it to the doorway. A customer lifted it gently and recognised its worn handle. The shopkeeper smiled. The old bell could remain part of the shop without being required to do its former work.
evidence_quotes: cracked bell beside the till rather than returning it to the doorway. A customer lifted it gently and recognised its worn handle. The shopkeeper smiled. The old bell could remain part of the shop without being required to do its former work.
stated_assumptions: The supplied literary passage is the complete evidence for this question.
option_analysis: A is incorrect because the passage says the old bell could remain part of the shop.
B is correct: the passage states that the bell could remain in the shop without doing its former work.
C is incorrect because the shopkeeper placed the cracked bell beside the till rather than returning it to the doorway.
D is incorrect because the passage distinguishes the quieter bell fitted after the crack from the cracked bell placed beside the till.

reasons: The passage says the old bell could remain part of the shop without being required to do its former work, which matches B.

body: A family was described as frugal after carefully limiting its grocery spending to the amount needed. Which word is closest in meaning to “frugal” in this sentence?
explanation: The sentence uses “frugal” to describe spending only what is needed on groceries. “Economical” is therefore the closest in meaning. “Transient” relates to short duration, “ambiguous” to having more than one meaning, and “meticulous” to attention to detail.

that can be understood in more than one way; having different meanings

body:
Rearrange the following four sentences to form a coherent account:
(A) After those votes had been counted, the teacher wrote the selected title on the story's cover.
(B) She collected their proposals and then read the complete list aloud.
(C) The process began when the teacher asked pupils to suggest titles for a shared story.
(D) Only after hearing that list did the class vote on the titles it contained.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: The coherent order is C-B-D-A: the teacher first asks for suggestions, then collects and reads the proposals, after which the class votes. The teacher writes the selected title only after those votes have been counted.
evidence_quotes: In a fictional class, the teacher first asked pupils to propose titles for a shared story. She collected their proposals and read the full list aloud. Only then did the class vote on the listed titles. After the votes had been counted, she wrote the selected title on the story's cover. This account establishes what
happened without claiming that a vote is always the best way to choose a title.
stated_assumptions: All four sentences describe the same teacher, class and title-selection process.
“Their proposals” refers to the titles suggested by the pupils, and “that list” refers to the list read aloud.
option_analysis: This order follows the stated progression from suggestions, to collecting and reading the proposals, to voting, and finally to writing the selected title on the cover.
This places the vote before the list is read, although sentence D says the class voted only after hearing that list.
This places the writing of the selected title before the class votes, although sentence A says it happened after those votes had been counted.
This places the collection and reading of the proposals before sentence C introduces the teacher and pupils to whom “She” and “their” refer.

body:
Which account best describes how the captains reached and implemented their decision?
A. The captains accepted Dev's correction without checking the recorded deliveries.
B. The captains replayed the match before changing the recorded result.
C. The captains checked the deliveries but kept the original result unchanged.
D. The captains checked the deliveries, agreed on the correction, and changed the result without replaying the match.
options: The captains accepted Dev's correction without checking the recorded deliveries.
The captains replayed the match before changing the recorded result.
The captains checked the deliveries but kept the original result unchanged.
The captains checked the deliveries, agreed on the correction, and changed the result without replaying the match.
explanation: The captains checked the recorded deliveries and agreed on the correction. They then changed the result without replaying the match, so D accurately describes both their decision and how they implemented it.
passage_text: Dev kept score during a friendly cricket match. As the players packed their bags, he noticed that he had counted one run twice. Correcting it would turn his team's victory into a tie. He showed the scorebook to the captains, who checked the recorded deliveries and agreed on the correction. One teammate said nobody would have noticed. Dev answered that noticing it himself was enough reason to check. The captains changed the result without replaying the match. On the walk home, Dev felt disappointed about the lost victory but relieved that the scorebook now matched the game.

body:
Which statements correctly describe comparative statements?
(A) They show a firm’s profitability and financial position for different periods in comparative form.
(B) The financial data are comparative only when the same accounting principles are used to prepare the statements.
(C) If accounting principles differ, the deviation should be mentioned in a footnote.
(D) Comparative analysis is also known as vertical analysis.
explanation: Statements (A), (B) and (C) correctly describe comparative statements: they present profitability and financial position across periods, require the same accounting principles for comparative data, and call for differences in accounting principles to be mentioned in a footnote. Statement (D) is incorrect because comparative analysis is also known as horizontal analysis.

body: On dissolution, A and B share profits and losses in the ratio 3:2. Immediately before recording the result of realisation, their capital accounts show credit balances of ₹2,60,000 and ₹2,00,000, respectively. The firm has non-cash assets with a book value of ₹5,00,000 and bank balance of ₹80,000; its only external liability is ₹1,20,000. All the non-cash assets are realised for ₹4,20,000, the liability is settled for ₹1,15,000, and realisation expenses of ₹10,000 are paid. There are no other assets, liabilities, expenses, reserves, partner loans, or capital movements. What amount should be paid to B on final settlement?
explanation: The realisation loss is ₹5,00,000 + ₹1,15,000 + ₹10,000 − ₹4,20,000 − ₹1,20,000 = ₹85,000. B’s share of this loss is 2/5 × ₹85,000 = ₹34,000, leaving a credit capital balance of ₹2,00,000 − ₹34,000 = ₹1,66,000. The adjusted balances of A and B total ₹3,75,000, equal to the bank balance remaining after the realisation transactions.
evidence_quotes: balance in this account is termed as profit or loss on realisation which is transferred to partners’ capital accounts in the profit sharing ratio (see figure 4.1). stated_assumptions: A and B’s stated capital balances are credit balances immediately before the realisation result is transferred.
The loss-sharing ratio is 3:2, with B entitled to 2/5 of any realisation loss.

The stated non-cash assets, bank balance and external liability are the firm’s only assets and liability; all non-cash assets are realised and the liability and expenses are paid in the amounts stated.
There are no other balances or transactions affecting the partners’ capital accounts or the bank balance.
option_analysis: ₹1,49,000 results from incorrectly allocating 3/5 of the realisation loss to B instead of 2/5.
₹1,66,000 is correct: B’s opening credit balance is reduced by his 2/5 share of the realisation loss.
₹2,00,000 leaves B’s opening capital unchanged and therefore omits the transfer of the realisation loss.
₹1,64,000 results from omitting the ₹5,000 saving when the ₹1,20,000 liability is settled for ₹1,15,000.

body: A company has ₹2,00,000 of uncalled capital, of which ₹50,000 is designated as Reserve Capital. The company is not being wound up and needs funds for its normal operations. Which statement applies to the ₹50,000?
options: It may be called only if the company is wound up.
It may be called during normal operations to meet the company’s operating need.
It may be called only after the winding-up process has been completed.
It may be called during normal operations if creditors request payment.
explanation: Reserve Capital is uncalled capital that may be called only in the event of winding up. Since the company is not being wound up and needs funds for normal operations, the ₹50,000 cannot be called for that purpose.
evidence_quotes: Reserve Capital: A company may reserve a portion of its uncalled capital to be called only in the event of winding up of the company. Such uncalled amount is called ‘Reserve Capital’ of the company. It is available only for the creditors on winding up of the company.
stated_assumptions: The ₹50,000 is a portion of the company's uncalled capital designated as Reserve Capital.
The company is not being wound up, and its stated funding need is for normal operations.
option_analysis: A is correct: the Reserve Capital may be called only in the event of winding up.
B is incorrect: the company's normal operating need is not the stated condition for calling Reserve Capital.
C is incorrect: the stated condition is winding up, not completion of the winding-up process.
D is incorrect: a creditors' request during normal operations does not satisfy the stated winding-up condition.

body:
Shares were issued at a premium. The stated shares in each case are forfeited for non-payment of call money. Match each case with the amount to be debited to Securities Premium Reserve Account at forfeiture. All amounts are in rupees.

List-I
(A) 400 shares; premium of ₹6 per share fully received
(B) 300 shares; premium of ₹5 per share wholly unpaid
(C) 250 shares; premium of ₹8 per share, of which ₹4 per share remains unpaid
(D) 200 shares; premium of ₹7 per share, of which ₹3 per share remains unpaid

List-II
(I) ₹0
(II) ₹600
(III) ₹1,000
(IV) ₹1,500

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Securities Premium Reserve Account is debited for the premium not received; no debit is made when the premium has been fully received. The amounts are A: ₹0, B: 300 × ₹5 = ₹1,500, C: 250 × ₹4 = ₹1,000, and D: 200 × ₹3 = ₹600. These amounts give the mapping in option A.

stated_assumptions: Each listed group consists entirely of shares forfeited for non-payment of call money.
The stated per-share amounts are the full premium due and the premium unpaid at forfeiture; no other premium-related amount is involved.
option_analysis: A is correct: the premium is fully received for case (A), while the unpaid premium amounts for (B), (C) and (D) are ₹1,500, ₹1,000 and ₹600 respectively.
B is incorrect: it assigns ₹1,000 to (B), whose unpaid premium is ₹1,500, and ₹1,500 to (C), whose unpaid premium is ₹1,000.
C is incorrect: it assigns a debit of ₹600 to (A), although its premium is fully received, and assigns no debit to (D), although ₹600 remains unpaid.
D is incorrect: it assigns ₹600 to (B), whose unpaid premium is ₹1,500, and ₹1,500 to (D), whose unpaid premium is ₹600.

supporting_spans.quote: Second and Final Call A/c 9,000 To Share Forfeiture A/c 15,000 (300 shares forfeited) Forfeiture of Shares issued at a Premium: If shares were initially issued at a premium and the premium amount has been fully realised, but some of the shares are forfeited due to non-payment of call money, the accounting treatment for forfeiture shall be on the same pattern as in the case of shares issued at par. The important point to be noted in this context is that the securities premium account is not to be debited at the time of forfeiture if the premium has been received in respect of the forefeited shares and the amount of forfeiture shall be

excluding premium amount. In case, however, if the premium amount has not been received, either wholly or partially, in respect of the shares forfeited, the Securities Premium Reserve Account will also be debited with the amount of premium not received along with the Share Capital Account at the time forfeiture. This will usually be the case when even the amount due on allotment has not been received. Thus, the journal entry to record the forfeiture of shares issued at a premium on which premium has not been fully received, will be : Share Capital A/c Dr. Securities Premium Reserve A/c Dr. To Share Forfeiture A/c Reprint 2026-27

(A) The comparative figures can indicate the trend and direction of the firm’s financial position and operating results.

body:
P and Q are the only existing partners and share profits in the ratio 3:2. R is admitted for 1/5 of the profits. No specific arrangement is made about how R acquires this share, so assume it is acquired from P and Q in their old profit-sharing ratio.

Arrange the following steps to determine the new profit-sharing ratio:
(A) Deduct the allocated sacrifices from P’s and Q’s old shares.
(B) Record the resulting shares of P, Q and R as 12/25, 8/25 and 1/5, respectively.
(C) Apportion R’s 1/5 share between P and Q in their old 3:2 ratio.
(D) Calculate P’s and Q’s respective sacrifices from R’s share as 3/25 and 2/25.

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: Since no specific arrangement is stated, R’s share is apportioned between P and Q in their old 3:2 ratio. Their sacrifices are 1/5 × 3/5 = 3/25 and 1/5 × 2/5 = 2/25; deducting these from their old shares gives 12/25 and 8/25. Thus the steps are (C)-(D)-(A)-(B), followed by recording all three shares in (B).
evidence_quotes: 2.3 New Profit Sharing Ratio When new partner is admitted he acquires his share in profits from the old partners. In other words, on the admission of a new partner, the old partners sacrifice a share of their profit in favour of the new partner. But, what will be the share of new partner and how he will acquire it from

the existing partners is decided mutually among the old partners and the new partner. However, if nothing is specified as to how does the new partner acquire his share from the old partners; it may be assumed that he gets it from them in their profit sharing ratio. In any case, on admission of a new partner, the

profit sharing ratio among the old partners will change keeping in view their respective contribution to the profit sharing ratio of the incoming partner. Hence, there is a need to ascertain the new profit sharing ratio among all the partners. This depends upon how does the new partner acquires his share from the old
partners for which there are many possibilities. Let us understand it with the help of the following illustrations.
stated_assumptions: P and Q are the only existing partners, and their old profit-sharing ratio is 3:2.
R is admitted for 1/5 of the profits.
No specific arrangement is made for how R acquires the share; assume R acquires it from P and Q in their old profit-sharing ratio.
option_analysis: A is incorrect because it calculates the sacrifices before establishing how R’s share is apportioned between P and Q.
B is correct: apportion R’s share, calculate each sacrifice, deduct the sacrifices from the old shares, and then state the resulting shares.
C is incorrect because it deducts the sacrifices before calculating their amounts.
D is incorrect because it begins by deducting sacrifices before apportioning R’s share or calculating the sacrifices.

(C) The partners reach the agreement on the business terms.

on loan, etc. The clauses of partnership deed can be altered with the consent of all the partners. The deed should be properly drafted and prepared as per the provisions of the ‘Stamp Act’ and preferably registered with the Registrar of Firms.

body:
At the beginning of an accounting period, a company has creditors of ₹1,20,000 and bills payable of ₹30,000. At the end of the period, it has creditors of ₹1,50,000 and bills payable of ₹50,000. Its trade payables turnover ratio for the period is exactly 5 times. What amount of purchases is represented by this ratio?
A. ₹1,75,000
B. ₹6,75,000
C. ₹8,75,000
D. ₹17,50,000
explanation: Average trade payables = (₹1,20,000 + ₹30,000 + ₹1,50,000 + ₹50,000) ÷ 2 = ₹1,75,000. Since the turnover ratio is purchases divided by average trade payables, purchases = 5 × ₹1,75,000 = ₹8,75,000.
evidence_quotes: 219Accounting Ratios Average Trade Payables = Creditors in the beginning + Bills payables in the beginning + Creditors at the end + Bills payables at the end 2 = Rs. 3,00,000 + Rs. 1,00,000 + Rs. 1,30,000 + Rs. 70,000 2 = Rs. 3,00,000 ∴ Trade Payables Turnover Ratio = Rs. 12,00,000 Rs. 3,00,000 = 4 times Illustration
stated_assumptions: The four balances given are the company’s complete creditors and bills payable balances at the beginning and end of the same accounting period.
The stated trade payables turnover ratio is exactly 5 times.
Purchases are calculated as the trade payables turnover ratio multiplied by average trade payables.
option_analysis: A is the average trade payables amount, but does not multiply it by the turnover ratio.
B results from excluding bills payable when calculating average trade payables, then multiplying by 5.
C uses all four balances to calculate average trade payables and multiplies the result by 5.
D multiplies the sum of all four balances by 5 without dividing that sum by 2.

Here, each item in the statement is stated as a percentage of the aggregate, or revenue from operations of which that item is a part. For example, a common size balance sheet shows

Inter-firm comparison or comparison of the company’s position with the related industry as a whole is

For example, revenue from operations may be taken as base (100) in case of statement of profit and loss and total assets or total liabilities (100) in case of balance sheet. 3. For all items of Col. 2 and 3 work out the percentage of that total. Column 4 and 5 shows these percentages in Exhibit 4.2. Common Size Statement Particulars Year Y ear Percentage

body:
A delivery service sets a standard average delivery time of 20 minutes per delivery. During one shift, 10 completed deliveries took 180 minutes in total. Treat actual performance as the mean time per delivery.

(A) The mean actual time was 18 minutes per delivery.
(B) The total actual time of 180 minutes can be compared directly with 20 minutes per delivery because both use minutes.
(C) Before comparison, actual performance should be expressed as 18 minutes per delivery.
(D) The comparison should be made in deliveries per shift rather than time per delivery.

Which statements are correct? Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The mean actual time is 180 ÷ 10 = 18 minutes per delivery, so (A) is correct. Expressing actual performance as 18 minutes per delivery gives it the same unit as the standard, so (C) is correct. (B) compares total time for 10 deliveries with time per delivery, while (D) changes the measure from time to deliveries.

The item asks only for the calculation and expression of actual performance for comparison; it does not ask whether the standard was met.
option_analysis: A: Correct. Dividing the total time, 180 minutes, by 10 deliveries gives 18 minutes per delivery.
B: Incorrect. It compares total time for 10 deliveries with time per delivery, so the measures are not expressed on the same basis.
C: Correct. Actual performance expressed as 18 minutes per delivery uses the same unit as the stated standard.
D: Incorrect. The standard is expressed as time per delivery, so deliveries per shift would not match its unit.

body: An organisation introduces a suitable monetary and non-monetary reward plan. An employee believes that their efforts will bring suitable rewards. Which response is supported by this situation?
options: The employee may contribute maximum efforts for the organisation.
The employee is assured of an attractive salary and monetary benefits.
The employee’s personal objectives become identical to the organisation’s objectives.
The employee can work without clear instructions from a manager.
explanation: When an employee believes that their efforts will bring suitable rewards, a good motivation plan can motivate them to contribute maximum efforts to the organisation. The situation does not establish that a particular salary is guaranteed, that personal and organisational objectives become identical, or that clear instructions are unnecessary.

stated_assumptions: Each described action is performed by a manager in an organisational setting.

Incorrect: this reverses instructing and guiding. Telling employees the steps is instructing, while showing an employee how to proceed is guiding.
Incorrect: this reverses counselling and motivating. Offering advice about a work concern represents counselling, while encouraging effort represents motivating.
Incorrect: it assigns counselling to giving task steps and guiding to advice about a work concern; it also assigns motivating to showing how to proceed and instructing to encouraging effort.

(D) The remuneration is just and equitable.

explanation: The two stated requirements are the basis for fair remuneration, which is described as just and equitable. Such remuneration ensures a congenial atmosphere and good relations; consequently, the company’s working is smooth. Thus, the supported order is (B)-(D)-(C)-(A).

stated_assumptions: The sequence begins with checking both stated remuneration requirements, as specified in the stem.
The item asks for the order of the requirements and the consequences described in the excerpt; no other case facts affect the sequence.
option_analysis: A is incorrect because it places the just-and-equitable characterisation before the checks that establish the stated remuneration requirements.
B is incorrect because it places the resulting atmosphere and relations before the remuneration is identified as just and equitable.
C is correct: the requirements are checked, remuneration is just and equitable, a congenial atmosphere and good relations result, and the company’s working is smooth.
D is incorrect because it places smooth working before the congenial atmosphere and good relations that precede it in the stated consequence.

body:
A company categorises four external developments as follows:
(i) A government authority issues an administrative order applicable to the company.
(ii) A court delivers a judgment concerning the company’s operations.
(iii) The government announces a change in the extent of its intervention in business.
(iv) Consumer preferences for the company’s product shift.

explanation: Government administrative orders and court judgments are included in the legal environment. The extent of government intervention in business is a political element, while consumer preferences are a social element; therefore, (i) and (ii) are the legal-environment pair.

body: A business uses resources that belong to society to make a household appliance. It can choose between two voluntary manufacturing practices: Practice X does not meet the needs and interests expressed by customers, while Practice Y does. The business chooses Practice Y, which is stated to serve the public interest and not impair public confidence. Which statement best explains how this choice relates to the business’s responsibility arising from its use of society’s resources?
options: This choice is justified because a business may set aside customer needs when it uses society’s resources to meet its own production aims.

This choice is justified because a business should voluntarily choose practices that take care of customer needs and interests, and supply products in the public interest without impairing public confidence.
This choice is justified because a business’s responsibility is confined to using society’s resources efficiently, while customer needs and public confidence are separate matters.
This choice is justified because a business need only take care of customer needs; public interest and public confidence do not affect its responsibility.
explanation: The case involves resources that belong to society. The stated responsibility is to supply products and services in the public interest without impairing public confidence, and voluntary practices should take care of customers’ needs and interests. body:
A manager identifies a production indicator as a critical point and sets a permissible limit for it. During review, one deviation is within the limit and routine in nature; another is significant and exceeds the limit. The manager intends to apply management by exception. Which statements are correct?
(A) Every departure from the standard must be referred to the manager, even when it remains within the permissible limit.
(B) The significant deviation that exceeds the permissible limit should be brought to the manager’s notice.
(C) The routine problem should be left to subordinates.
(D) Once a significant deviation is referred to the manager, its cause need not be analysed.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Management by exception directs managerial attention to significant deviations that exceed the permissible limit, while routine problems are left to subordinates. The deviations requiring managerial attention must also be analysed for their causes, so statement (D) is incorrect.

body: Which statement correctly describes the general nature and role of principles of management?
options: They are general workplace guidelines usable under certain situations that help managers take and implement decisions.
They are Taylor’s scientific-management principles, including science, harmony, cooperation and maximum output.
They are Taylor’s scientific-management techniques, including functional foremanship, standardisation and method study.
They are Fayol’s management functions, including planning, organising, command, coordination and control.
explanation: Principles of management are general guidelines for workplace conduct under certain situations, and they help managers take and implement decisions. Options B, C and D refer respectively to Taylor’s scientific-management principles, Taylor’s techniques and Fayol’s functions.
evidence_quotes: 64 Business Studies Summary Meaning Principles of management are general guidelines, which can be used for conduct in work places under certain situations. They help managers to take and implement decisions. Nature The nature of management principles can be discussed under the heads- formed by practice; general

guidelines; universal; flexible; behavioural; contingent; and cause and effect relationship Significance Proper understanding of significance of management principles is essential to make sound decisions by managers. The significance can be discussed under the following heads- Increase in efficiency; Optimum

utilisation of resources; Scientific decision making; Adaptation to changing environment; Fulfilling social responsibilities; Proper research and development; Training managers; and Effective administration. Scientific Management Taylor’s principles of scientific management are — Science, not the rule of thumb;

Harmony not discord; Cooperation not individualism; Maximum not restricted output; Development of each person to her/ his greatest efficiency and prosperity. The techniques of scientific management as per Taylor were — Functional foremanship; Standardisation and simplification of work; Fatigue Study; Method Study;
stated_assumptions: The case-note labels identify each action with the Fayol function named in it; no additional interpretation of the actions is needed.
The requested sequence is the order in which the functions are listed, not a claim that every management situation must follow a temporal sequence.
The four actions represent the first four functions in Fayol’s list; the fifth function, control, is not included among the actions.
option_analysis: A is correct: P, Q, R and S correspond to plan, organise, command and coordinate, in the order Fayol lists them.
B is incorrect: it places command before organise, whereas Fayol lists organise before command.
C is incorrect: it places organise before plan, whereas Fayol lists plan first.
D is incorrect: it places coordinate before command, whereas Fayol lists command before coordinate.

body: A unit’s review records show that its targets were met according to plans. Employees report being happy and satisfied, and work proceeds in an orderly way rather than in chaos. An observer can see these outcomes but cannot see management as an object. Which interpretation best explains the case?
options: Management is tangible because the supervisors who carry it out can be seen.
Management is intangible; its presence is felt through how the unit functions and the outcomes described.
Management itself is directly visible because targets, employee responses and orderly operations can be observed.
Management’s presence is indicated by target attainment alone; employee satisfaction and orderliness do not indicate its effect.
explanation: Management is described as a force that cannot be seen, while its presence can be felt through the way an organisation functions. The case includes the stated signs of its effect: targets met according to plans, employee satisfaction and orderliness. These observable outcomes indicate management’s presence; they do not make management itself visible.
evidence_quotes: (vii) Management is an intangible force: Management is an intangi - ble force that cannot be seen but its presence can be felt in the way the organisation functions. The effect of management is noticeable in an organisation where targets are met according to plans, employees are happy and satisfied, and there is
orderliness instead of chaos.
stated_assumptions: The review records and employee reports accurately describe the unit’s functioning.
Management in the question refers to the force affecting the unit’s functioning, not to the physical presence of an individual manager.
option_analysis: A is incorrect because the physical visibility of supervisors does not make management itself tangible.
B is correct: the force is not seen, but its presence is felt through the unit’s functioning and the listed outcomes.
C is incorrect because the outcomes may be observed, but management itself is described as unseen.
D is incorrect because employee satisfaction and orderliness, as well as target attainment according to plans, are stated signs of management’s effect.

body:
A firm groups its production, finance and marketing employees by function. Employees doing similar tasks coordinate smoothly within each department. However, each functional head prioritises that department’s interests over a stated enterprise-wide objective, and interaction between production and marketing has weakened.
Consider the following statements:
(A) Smooth coordination within departments does not rule out coordination problems between functionally differentiated departments.
(B) Similarity of tasks within a department guarantees that each functional head prioritises enterprise-wide objectives.
(C) Pursuing departmental interests at the expense of organisational interests can hinder interaction between departments.
(D) Smooth coordination within functions necessarily eliminates coordination problems across functions.
Which statements correctly interpret the situation?
explanation: The case illustrates that coordination within a department can coexist with problems between functionally differentiated departments. It also reflects the risk that pursuing departmental interests at the expense of organisational interests can hinder interaction. Thus, statements (A) and (C) are supported; the case does not support the guarantees asserted in (B) and (D).
evidence_quotes: Disadvantages: The functional structur e has certain disadvantages which an organisation must take into consideration before it adopts it. Some of them are as follows: (a) A functional structure places less emphasis on overall enterprise objectives than the objectives pursued by a functional head. Such practices may

lead to functional empires wherein the importance of a particular function may be overemphasised. Pursuing departmental interests at the cost of organisational interests can also hinder the interaction between two or more departments. (b) It may lead to problems in coordination as information has to be exchanged
stated_assumptions: The firm’s production, finance and marketing departments are organised by function, and the employees doing similar tasks coordinate smoothly within each department.

The functional heads prioritise their departments’ interests over the stated enterprise-wide objective, and interaction between production and marketing has weakened; these are stipulated case facts, not universal claims about functional structures.
option_analysis: Correct. Statements (A) and (C) fit the case and the stated risk that departmental interests can hinder interaction across departments.
Incorrect. Statement (D) asserts that smooth coordination within functions necessarily eliminates cross-functional coordination problems, contrary to the weakened interaction stipulated in the case.
Incorrect. Statement (B) is contradicted by the case fact that each functional head prioritises departmental interests over the enterprise-wide objective.
Incorrect. Statements (B) and (D) both make claims that are contradicted by the case facts.

body:
A manager seeks to replace traditional work methods with one standard method. The manager considers these actions:
I. Follow the standard method throughout the organisation
II. Investigate traditional methods through work-study
III. Develop a standard method
IV. Unify the best practices

Which sequence arranges the actions from first to last?
explanation: The process begins with investigating traditional methods through work-study, followed by unifying the best practices and developing a standard method. The standard method is then followed throughout the organisation, giving the sequence II, IV, III, I.

body: A firm’s two units use the same technology and face comparable operating conditions, but the quality of their human resources differs. When assessing their capacity to achieve organisational goals, which principle should guide the assessment?
options: The assessment should account for the quality of the units’ human resources.
The assessment should account only for the condition of the units’ equipment.
The assessment should treat staffing as limited to employees’ salaries, welfare and working conditions.
The assessment should consider human-resource quality only after organisational goals are achieved.
explanation: An organisation’s ability to achieve its goals depends upon the quality of its human resources. Therefore, that quality should be considered when assessing the units’ capacity to achieve their goals.

body:
Meera is using a household product. Before using it, she reads and follows the manufacturer’s instructions. She continues to acquire knowledge about products over time and aims to remain well informed throughout life.

Consider the following statements:
(A) Meera’s use of the manufacturer’s instructions is consistent with using the product safely.
(B) The guidance treats acquiring knowledge as a task completed once, rather than continued throughout life.
(C) Continuing to acquire knowledge is consistent with becoming well informed throughout life.
(D) The guidance treats access to manufacturer’s instructions and acquiring knowledge as alternatives, so a consumer needs only one of them.

Which statements are supported by the guidance described?
(A) (A) and (B) only
(B) (B) and (D) only
(C) (A) and (D) only
(D) (A) and (C) only
explanation: The guidance connects manufacturer’s instructions with safe product use and calls for acquiring knowledge and being well informed throughout life. Statements (A) and (C) are consistent with these ideas; (B) contradicts lifelong learning, while (D) incorrectly presents the two ideas as alternatives.

He should be (iv) Read labels carefully so as to aware about his rights and the have information about prices, net weight, manufacturing and reliefs available
stated_assumptions: The case stipulates that Meera reads and follows the manufacturer’s instructions before using the product and continues acquiring knowledge over time.
The statements are assessed only against the guidance in the supplied excerpt; no product-specific instructions or outside standards are assumed.
option_analysis: (A) Incorrect. It includes statement (B), which conflicts with the lifelong-learning guidance, and omits supported statement (C).
(B) Incorrect. Statements (B) and (D) each conflict with the guidance; it also omits supported statements (A) and (C).
(C) Incorrect. It includes unsupported statement (D) and omits supported statement (C).
(D) Correct. Statements (A) and (C) reflect the guidance on instructions, safe use and acquiring knowledge throughout life.

(A) Actual results are consolidated in performance reports.

List-II
(I) Use a stated technique for measuring actual performance.
(II) Use the same units for actual performance and the standard.
(III) Measure work during performance where possible.
(IV) Ensure that actual performance is measured objectively and reliably.

body: A development agency compares two countries using an index that includes only GDP per capita, literacy, life expectancy and mortality rates. The countries receive equal index values. The index contains no measure of constitutional protection of citizens’ rights, independence of the judiciary or the rule of law. Which conclusion about the comparison is best supported?
options: Equal index values establish that the countries have equal overall levels of development.
Equal index values provide only a limited comparison of overall development because important institutional dimensions are omitted.
Equal index values provide a complete comparison because the index covers income, education and health.
Equal index values provide no useful comparison because the index omits institutional dimensions.

By how many lakh does the estimated number of tertiary/service-sector workers in the urban group exceed the estimated number in the rural group?

The listed real per capita income values are ₹7,651 in 1951, ₹12,174 in 1981, ₹15,748 in 1991, ₹23,095 in 2001 and ₹94,054 in 2018–22. For each interval, calculate the increase by subtracting the earlier listed value from the later one; do not annualise the 2001–2018–22 difference.

(A) The increase from 1991 to 2001 was ₹7,347.
(B) The increase from 1981 to 1991 was ₹4,523.
(C) The increase from 2001 to 2018–22 was ₹70,959.
(D) The increase from 1951 to 1981 was ₹3,574.

Which of the above statements are correct?
explanation: The increases from 1991 to 2001 and from 2001 to 2018–22 are ₹23,095 − ₹15,748 = ₹7,347 and ₹94,054 − ₹23,095 = ₹70,959, respectively, so (A) and (C) are correct. The increase from 1981 to 1991 is ₹3,574, while the increase from 1951 to 1981 is ₹4,523; (B) and (D) assign these amounts to the wrong intervals.

body:
A producer plans to add ₹1,20,000 to inventory by the end of the year. To meet extra demand, she later sells goods worth ₹35,000 from that inventory. Assume no other changes to inventory occur. Arrange the following events and steps in the order that leads from the producer’s plan to identifying actual investment.
(A) The producer plans an addition of ₹1,20,000 to inventory.
(B) The producer sells ₹35,000 worth of goods from inventory to meet extra demand.
(C) The net increase in inventory is calculated as ₹1,20,000 − ₹35,000 = ₹85,000.
(D) The amount of ₹85,000 is identified as actual (ex post) investment.
Choose the correct sequence:
A. (A)-(C)-(B)-(D)
B. (B)-(A)-(C)-(D)
C. (A)-(B)-(C)-(D)
D. (A)-(B)-(D)-(C)
explanation: The planned addition is ₹1,20,000, and the later sale from inventory reduces the net increase by ₹35,000. Thus, actual investment is ₹1,20,000 − ₹35,000 = ₹85,000. The plan and sale must be accounted for before calculating and identifying the actual investment.

body: A review of India reports that the population share working in agriculture was 67.5% in 1950 and 64.9% in 1990. Industry’s share of GDP was 13% in 1950–51 and 24.6% in 1990–91, and the industrial sector’s annual growth rate during the period was 6%. The review also reports that industry and services did not absorb the people working in agriculture. A commentator concludes that the rise in industry’s GDP share demonstrates a comparable transfer of workers from agriculture to industry. Which assessment follows from the stated facts?

body: A consumer's total utility from consuming 1, 2 and 3 units of commodity X is 10, 18 and 24 utils, respectively. Consumption of all other commodities is unchanged. Which interpretation of the marginal utility of the second and third units, respectively, is correct?
options: Marginal utility rises from 10 to 18 utils, while total utility rises from 18 to 24 utils.
Marginal utility rises from 8 to 14 utils, while total utility rises from 18 to 24 utils.
Marginal utility falls from 8 to 6 utils, while total utility rises from 18 to 24 utils.
Marginal utility remains at 8 utils, while total utility rises from 18 to 24 utils.
explanation: Marginal utility is the change in total utility when consumption increases by one unit. It is 18 − 10 = 8 utils for the second unit and 24 − 18 = 6 utils for the third; total utility rises from 18 to 24 utils.

stated_assumptions: The stated total utility figures correspond to consumption of exactly 1, 2 and 3 units of commodity X.

option_analysis: A is incorrect because it treats the total utility levels at 1 and 2 units as the marginal utilities of the second and third units.
B is incorrect because 24 − 10 spans an increase of two units; it is not the marginal utility of the third unit alone.
C is correct: the one-unit increases in total utility are 18 − 10 = 8 and 24 − 18 = 6 utils.
D is incorrect because the marginal utility of the third unit is the change from total utility at 2 units to total utility at 3 units, which is 6 utils.

body: In one open-market session, the RBI purchases Government bonds for ₹1,80,000 and sells Government bonds to private institutions for ₹65,000. Both transactions are settled by cheques. For this question, count each cheque amount as an immediate, rupee-for-rupee change in reserves, and assume no other changes in reserves during the session. What is the net change in reserves?
explanation: The purchase adds ₹1,80,000 to reserves, while the sale withdraws ₹65,000. The net change is ₹1,80,000 − ₹65,000 = ₹1,15,000, an increase.
evidence_quotes: When RBI buys a Government bond in the open market, it pays for it by giving a cheque. This cheque increases the total amount of reserves in the economy and thus increases the money supply. Selling of a bond by RBI (to private individuals or institutions) leads to reduction in quantity of reserves and hence the money
stated_assumptions: Each transaction's cheque amount equals its immediate change in reserves.
No other changes in reserves occur during the session.
option_analysis: Correct: subtracts the reserve outflow from the bond sale from the reserve inflow from the purchase.
Adds the purchase and sale amounts, treating the sale as an inflow rather than an outflow.
Counts the sale-related outflow but omits the purchase-related inflow.
Counts the purchase-related inflow but omits the sale-related outflow.

body:
In an income-determination example, the marginal propensity to consume (MPC) is 0.8. For each statement, assume that the change in consumption expenditure arises only from the stated increase in income.

(I) An income increase of ₹50 raises consumption expenditure by ₹40.
(II) An income increase of ₹100 raises consumption expenditure by ₹80.
(III) An income increase of ₹50 raises consumption expenditure by ₹50.
(IV) An MPC of 0.8 means that consumption expenditure is 80% of total income.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: MPC of 0.8 means that 0.8 of additional income is spent on consumption. Thus, the increases of ₹50 and ₹100 raise consumption expenditure by ₹40 and ₹80, respectively, making (I) and (II) correct. Statement (III) uses the full income increase, while (IV) applies the ratio to total income rather than additional income.
evidence_quotes: When income increases by 10, consumption expenditure goes up by (0.8)10, since people spend 0.8 (= mpc) fraction of their additional income on consumption.
stated_assumptions: MPC is 0.8 in each case.
Consumption expenditure changes only in response to the stated increase in income.
The stated amounts are increases in income, and the question asks about the resulting increases in consumption expenditure.
option_analysis: Incorrect: statement (III) is false because 0.8 × ₹50 = ₹40, not ₹50.
Incorrect: statement (IV) is false because the 0.8 ratio applies to additional income, not total income.
Correct: statements (I) and (II) follow from applying 0.8 to the stated additional incomes.
Incorrect: both statements (III) and (IV) are false for the reasons stated above.

body: A catalogue entry describes a textile as cotton muslin from Bengal and records a foreign traveller’s label, “malmal khas”. No surviving record identifies who wore this particular textile. What does the label imply?
options: It indicates that the textile is silk rather than cotton.
It indicates that the muslin is an ordinary variety rather than the finest variety.
It indicates that a particular royal person actually wore this textile.
It indicates that the textile was worn by, or fit for, royalty.
explanation: Malmal was the finest variety of muslin, and “malmal khas” implied that it was worn by, or fit for, royalty. The label expresses a royal association; it does not establish that a particular royal person actually wore this textile.

country’s economic past even as you learn about its present state and future prospects. So, let us first look at the state of India’s economy prior to the country’s independence and form an idea of the various considerations that shaped India’ s post-independence development strategy. The structure of India’s present-

day economy is not just of current making; it has its roots steeped in history, particularly in the period when India was under British rule which lasted for almost two centuries before India finally won its independence on 15 August 1947. The sole purpose of the British colonial rule in India was to reduce the

country to being a raw material supplier for Great Britain’s own rapidly expanding modern industrial base. body: A government sets a price ceiling below the equilibrium price for a commodity and rations the available quantity through ration shops. Which outcome is identified for consumers in this situation?
options: Each consumer has to stand in long queues to buy the good from ration shops.
Every consumer receives the full quantity they want from ration shops.
Consumers who are not satisfied with the quantity received are unwilling to pay a higher price for the good.
Excess supply arises because firms offer more than consumers demand at the ceiling price.
explanation: A is correct: when a below-equilibrium price ceiling is accompanied by rationing, consumers have to stand in long queues at ration shops. The ceiling leads to excess demand, not excess supply; the stated outcomes also include that some consumers may remain unsatisfied and be willing to pay a higher price.

average cost of the firms. • With free entry and exit, the shift in demand has no impact on equilibrium price but changes the equilibrium quantity and number of firms in the same direction as the change in demand. • In comparison to a market with fixed number of firms, the impact of a shift in demand curve on

equilibrium quantity is more pronounced in a market with free entry and exit. • Imposition of price ceiling below the equilibrium price leads to an excess demand. • Imposition of price floor above the equilibrium price leads to an excess supply. Reprint 2026-27

body:
Match each central-bank action in List-I with its corresponding implication in List-II.

List-I
(A) The RBI buys a Government bond in the open market and pays by cheque.
(B) The RBI sells a Government bond to a private individual or institution.
(C) The RBI raises the reserve ratio.
(D) The central bank uses moral suasion to encourage commercial banks to lend.

List-II
(I) Increases reserves and, consequently, money supply.
(II) Reduces reserves and, consequently, money supply.
(III) Reduces banks’ lending and money supply when the reserve ratio is raised.
(IV) Uses qualitative persuasion to encourage commercial-bank lending.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: When the RBI buys a Government bond and pays by cheque, reserves and money supply increase; selling a bond reduces reserves and money supply. Raising the reserve ratio reduces banks’ lending and money supply. Moral suasion is qualitative persuasion that can be used to encourage commercial-bank lending.
evidence_quotes: POLICY TOOLS TO CO NTROL MONEY SUPPLY Reserve Bank is the only institution which can issue currency. When commercial banks need more funds in order to be able to create more credit, they may go to market for such funds or go to the Central Bank. Central bank provides them funds through various instruments. This role
stated_assumptions: Each item describes one central-bank action; the implications are matched to the actions as stated, without assuming any other policy change.
option_analysis: Incorrect: it reverses the effects of the RBI buying and selling Government bonds; the other two matches are correct.
Correct: bond purchases increase reserves and money supply, bond sales reduce them, a higher reserve ratio reduces lending and money supply, and moral suasion can encourage lending.
Incorrect: it assigns the bond-sale implication to a higher reserve ratio and assigns a fall in reserves to the higher reserve ratio; the stated implications distinguish these actions.
Incorrect: it assigns qualitative persuasion to a reserve-ratio change and assigns reduced lending to moral suasion that is specified as encouraging lending.

source_support.syllabus_topic: Central-bank policy tools to control money supply: open-market operations, reserve-ratio changes, and qualitative tools such as moral suasion

answer_conditions.condition: The RBI buys a Government bond in the open market and pays by cheque.
The RBI sells a Government bond to a private individual or institution.
The central bank raises the reserve ratio.
The central bank uses moral suasion to encourage commercial-bank lending.

supporting_spans.quote: Quantitative tools, control the extent of money supply by changing the CRR, or bank rate or open market operations. Qualitative tools include persuasion by the Central bank in order to make commercial banks discourage or encourage lending which is done through moral suasion, margin requirement, etc. It should be evident by now that if the Central bank changes the reserve ratio, this would lead to changes in lending by the banks which, in turn, would impact the deposits and hence, the money supply. In the previously discussed example, what would the money multiplier be if the RBI increases the reserve ratio to 25 per cent? Notice that in the

previous case, Rs 100 in reserves could support deposits of Rs 400. But the banking system would now be able to loan Rs 300 only. It would have to call back some loans to meet the increased reserve requirements. Hence, money supply would fall. Another important tool by which the RBI also influences money supply is Open Market Operations. Open Market Operations refers to buying and selling of bonds issued by the Government in the open market. This purchase and sale is entrusted to the Central bank on behalf of the Government. When RBI buys a Government bond in the open market, it pays for it by giving a cheque. This cheque increases the total

amount of reserves in the economy and thus increases the money supply. Selling of a bond by RBI (to private individuals or institutions) leads to reduction in quantity of reserves and hence the money supply. There are two types of open market operations: outright and repo. Outright open market operations are permanent in nature: when the central bank buys these securities (thus injecting money into the system), it is without any promise to sell them later. body:
Consider a two-sector circular-flow diagram containing only households and firms. The goods-and-services market is shown above the factor market. The upper pair of arrows represents flows in the goods-and-services market, and the lower pair represents flows in the factor market. Select the correct statements about the arrows.
(A) The uppermost arrow, from households to firms, represents household payments for goods and services.
(B) The arrow immediately below it, from firms to households, represents factor payments.
(C) The lowest arrow, from households to firms, represents factor services supplied by households.
(D) The arrow immediately above the lowest one, from firms to households, represents goods and services supplied to households.
explanation: In the upper pair, the arrow from households to firms represents spending on goods and services, while the reverse arrow represents goods and services supplied by firms. In the lower pair, the arrow from households to firms represents factor services, and the reverse arrow represents payments for those services. Therefore, statements (A) and (C) are correct.
evidence_quotes: 15 1515 1515National Income Accounting entire income of the economy, therefore, comes back to the producers in the form of sales revenue. There is no leakage from the system – there is no difference between the amount that the firms had distributed in the form of factor payments (which is the sum total of remunerations

earned by the four factors of production) and the aggregate consumption expenditure that they receive as sales revenue. In the next period the firms will once again produce goods and services and pay remunerations to the factors of production. These remunerations will once again be used to buy the goods and services.

Hence year after year we can imagine the aggregate income of the economy going through the two sectors, firms and households, in a circular way. This is represented in Fig. 2.1. When the income is being spent on the goods and services produced by the firms, it takes the form of aggregate expenditure received by the

firms. Since the value of expenditure must be equal to the value of goods and services, we can equivalently measure the aggregate income by “calculating the aggregate value of goods and services pr oduced by the fir ms”. When the aggr egate revenue received by the firms is paid out to the factors of production it

Incorrect. Statement (B) misidentifies the arrow immediately below the uppermost arrow, which represents goods and services flowing from firms to households.
Incorrect. Statements (B) and (D) misidentify the two flows: the upper goods-market return flow is goods and services, while the arrow above the lowest one is factor payments.
Incorrect. Statement (D) misidentifies the arrow above the lowest one, which represents payments from firms to households for factor services.

body: A firm is operating in the short run. At an output of 4 units, its total cost is ₹74 and its total fixed cost is ₹31. It increases output from 4 to 7 units. The short-run marginal costs of the 5th, 6th and 7th units are ₹7, ₹9 and ₹11, respectively. Assuming total fixed cost remains unchanged, what is the firm's total cost at 7 units of output?
